topics.title: 1. Basic Formulas & Cell Referencing
topics.content:
Understanding cell references is the foundation of Excel, and a guaranteed interview question.

  • Relative Reference (A1): Changes when you copy the formula to another cell.
  • Absolute Reference ($A$1): Locked entirely. Does not change when dragged down or across. Press F4 to toggle.
  • Mixed Reference ($A1 or A$1): Locks either the column ($A) or the row ($1). Crucial for creating 2D matrices like multiplication tables.
topics.code:
Relative: =A1 * B1
Absolute: =A1 * $B$1
Mixed (Lock Row): =A1 * B$1
Mixed (Lock Col): =$A1 * B1

Shortcut: Press F4 while editing a formula to cycle through lock modes.
topics.output:
Relative changes to A2*B2 when dragged down.
Absolute keeps multiplying by B1.

topics.title: 2. Logical Functions (IF, AND, OR, IFS)
topics.content:
Logical functions evaluate conditions and return specific outputs. They are heavily tested in data screening tasks.

  • IF: =IF(logical_test, value_if_true, value_if_false)
  • AND / OR: Used inside an IF statement to test multiple conditions. AND() requires ALL conditions to be true. OR() requires at least ONE condition to be true.
  • IFS (Excel 2019+): Replaces messy "Nested IFs" by checking multiple conditions sequentially.
topics.code:
# Basic IF
=IF(B2>=60, "Pass", "Fail")

# Nested with AND
=IF(AND(B2>=60, C2>=90), "High Pass", "Standard")

# Using IFS (modern approach)
=IFS(B2>=90, "A", B2>=80, "B", B2>=70, "C", TRUE, "F")
coding_questions: Write a formula that returns 'Bonus' if Sales > 10000 AND Rating >= 4, otherwise return 'No Bonus'.
Use the IFS function to categorize ages: <18 as 'Minor', 18-64 as 'Adult', and >=65 as 'Senior'.

quiz.question: What is the maximum number of IF functions you can nest in modern Excel?

topics.title: 3. Lookup Functions (VLOOKUP, INDEX-MATCH)
topics.content:
The Holy Grail of Excel Interviews. You MUST master these to pass an Excel assessment.

  • VLOOKUP: =VLOOKUP(lookup_value, table_array, col_index, [range_lookup]). Always use FALSE or 0 for exact match. Limitation: It can only search from left to right.
  • INDEX-MATCH: The professional alternative. MATCH() finds the row number, INDEX() returns the value from that row. It can search left, right, up, or down dynamically.
  • XLOOKUP: The modern replacement. =XLOOKUP(lookup_value, lookup_array, return_array).
topics.code:
# VLOOKUP (Exact Match)
=VLOOKUP("EMP102", A2:D100, 3, FALSE)

# INDEX & MATCH (Dynamic & robust against column insertions)
=INDEX(C2:C100, MATCH("EMP102", A2:A100, 0))

# XLOOKUP (With built-in 'if not found' handler)
=XLOOKUP("EMP102", A2:A100, C2:C100, "Not Found")
topics.output:
Returns Employee Name from Column 3.
Returns exact match regardless of column order.
coding_questions: Write a VLOOKUP formula to find the Price (3rd column) of a Product ID located in cell G2 from the table A1:D50.
Write an INDEX-MATCH formula to find a 'Manager Name' (Column A) based on an 'Employee ID' (Column D) (A left-lookup task).

quiz.question: What happens if you use TRUE for the 4th argument in VLOOKUP?
options: It returns an approximate match (requires sorted data)

quiz.question: Why do analysts prefer INDEX-MATCH over VLOOKUP?
options: It doesn't break if you insert a new column
It can search left to right

topics.title: 4. Data Aggregation (SUMIFS, COUNTIFS)
topics.content:
Used to summarize data based on specific conditions. Essential for building dashboards.

  • COUNTIFS: Counts rows that meet one or more criteria.
  • SUMIFS: Adds values in a range that meet one or more criteria. Syntax Rule: In SUMIFS, the Sum_Range is always the FIRST argument.
  • Wildcards: Use * (any number of characters) or ? (single character) in your criteria to match partial text (e.g., "*Apple*" matches "Red Apple Inc").
topics.code:
# COUNTIFS
=COUNTIFS(Region_Col, "North", Sales_Col, ">5000")

# SUMIFS (Sum Range is FIRST)
=SUMIFS(Revenue_Col, Region_Col, "South", Status_Col, "Completed")

# Using Wildcards
=SUMIFS(Revenue_Col, Item_Col, "*Shirt*")
topics.output:
Counts rows where North sales > 5000.
Sums Revenue where Region is South AND Status is Completed.
coding_questions: Write a SUMIFS formula to sum the 'Profit' column where 'Year' is 2023 and 'Department' is 'HR'.
Write a COUNTIFS formula to count how many employees have 'Manager' anywhere in their job title.

quiz.question: In the SUMIFS function, where does the range you want to sum go?

topics.title: 5. Text Manipulation & Data Cleaning
topics.content:
"Data Cleansing" is a standard interview test. You must know how to clean messy data.

  • TRIM & PROPER: TRIM() removes accidental leading/trailing spaces. PROPER() capitalizes the first letter of each word.
  • LEFT, RIGHT, MID: Extracts a specific number of characters from a text string.
  • FIND & SEARCH: Locates the position of a character. SEARCH() is case-insensitive, FIND() is case-sensitive.
  • TEXTJOIN: Better than CONCATENATE because it allows you to specify a delimiter (like a comma) and ignore empty cells.
topics.code:
# Clean Messy Data
=TRIM(PROPER(A2))

# Extract first 3 characters
=LEFT(A2, 3)

# Extract Username from Email (Dynamic extraction)
=LEFT(A2, FIND("@", A2) - 1)

# Combine text
=TEXTJOIN(", ", TRUE, A2, B2, C2)
topics.output:
john doe  -> John Doe
john@mail.com -> john
Apple, Banana, Cherry
coding_questions: Write a formula to extract the domain name (everything AFTER the '@') from an email address in cell A2.

topics.title: 6. Date & Time Functions
topics.content:
Excel stores dates as serial numbers (Day 1 is Jan 1, 1900). Understanding this solves many date calculation errors.

  • TODAY() / NOW(): Returns the current date / current date + time. (Volatile functions that recalculate daily).
  • EOMONTH: Returns the last day of the month, X months in the past or future. Great for financial modeling.
  • NETWORKDAYS: Calculates the number of working days between two dates, automatically excluding weekends and optionally, a list of custom holidays.
topics.code:
# Current Date
=TODAY()

# Last day of the CURRENT month
=EOMONTH(TODAY(), 0)

# Last day of NEXT month
=EOMONTH(TODAY(), 1)

# Working days between Project Start (A2) and End (B2)
=NETWORKDAYS(A2, B2, Holidays_Range)
coding_questions: Write a formula to find the exact date 90 days from today.
Write a formula to calculate the number of working days a project took, assuming Start Date is in A2, End Date is in B2, and holidays are in Z1:Z10.

topics.title: 7. Pivot Tables & Advanced Data Modeling
topics.content:
Pivot tables summarize hundreds of thousands of rows in seconds. A mandatory skill for any analyst role.

  • Best Practices: Ensure no blank column headers. Convert your data range to an Excel Table (Ctrl+T) first, so the Pivot Table updates automatically when new data is added.
  • Grouping: Right-click a date in a Pivot Table and select 'Group' to instantly summarize by Month, Quarter, or Year.
  • Calculated Fields: Create new formulas INSIDE the pivot table (e.g., = Profit / Revenue) rather than adding columns to the raw data.
  • Power Pivot: Used to handle millions of rows and create relationships between multiple tables (Relational database logic within Excel).
topics.code:
Steps to create a dynamic Pivot:
1. Click anywhere in data.
2. Press Ctrl + T to make a Table.
3. Insert -> Pivot Table.
4. Drag 'Region' to Rows.
5. Drag 'Revenue' to Values.
6. Insert -> Slicer (Choose Region).

topics.title: 8. Dashboards & Advanced Charts
topics.content:
Visualizing data effectively is key to a corporate presentation.

  • Combo Charts: Used to plot two different types of data on the same chart (e.g., Revenue as Bars, Profit Margin as a Line). Always use a Secondary Axis for the percentage.
  • Dynamic Dashboards: Built by connecting Pivot Charts to Slicers and Timelines. One slicer can control multiple charts via 'Report Connections'.
  • Form Controls: (Found in the Developer tab) Checkboxes, Radio buttons, and Combo Boxes can be linked to cells to make your dashboard highly interactive without using VBA.
  • Sparklines: Mini charts placed inside a single cell to show a quick trend.
topics.code:
Steps for a Combo Chart:
1. Select data -> Insert -> Recommended Charts -> All Charts -> Combo.
2. Set Series 1 (Revenue) to Clustered Column.
3. Set Series 2 (Margin) to Line.
4. CHECK the box for 'Secondary Axis' next to Margin.
topics.output: A chart with bars and a trendline, using two different Y-axes.

options: An interactive visual filter for Pivot Tables and Charts

topics.title: 9. VBA & Macros (Excel Codes)
topics.content:
Visual Basic for Applications (VBA) automates repetitive tasks.

  • Macro Recorder: The easiest way to learn VBA. It records your clicks and translates them into code.
  • The Developer Tab: Must be enabled via Options > Customize Ribbon. Press Alt + F11 to open the VBA Editor.
  • VBA Syntax Basics: Code is stored in Modules. Procedures start with Sub and end with End Sub.
  • Referencing Cells: Range("A1").Value = "Hello" or Cells(1, 1).Value = "Hello".
  • Loops in VBA: For i = 1 to 10 ... Next i is used to loop through rows automatically.
topics.code:
Sub ClearData()
    ' This is a VBA comment
    ' Clears contents of A1 to A10
    Range("A1:A10").ClearContents
    MsgBox "Data Cleared Successfully!"
End Sub

Sub SimpleLoop()
    Dim i As Integer
    For i = 1 To 5
        Cells(i, 1).Value = "Test " & i
    Next i
End Sub
topics.output:
A pop-up box says 'Data Cleared Successfully!'.
Cells A1 to A5 are filled with 'Test 1' to 'Test 5'.

topics.title: 10. Advanced Tools (Goal Seek, Power Query)
topics.content:
These tools handle data modeling and complex problem-solving.

  • Goal Seek: Works backward. If you know the result you want a formula to produce, Goal Seek finds the input value required to achieve it.
  • Power Query: The ultimate data cleaning tool. Allows you to import data from folders, websites, or SQL databases, clean it step-by-step, and load it into Excel. It saves the steps, so next time you just hit 'Refresh'.
  • Remove Duplicates: Instantly deletes identical rows based on selected columns.
topics.code:
Goal Seek Example:
1. Data Tab -> What-If Analysis -> Goal Seek
2. Set Cell: [Formula Cell]
3. To Value: [Target Number]
4. By changing cell: [Input Cell]

Power Query M-Code (Conceptual):
= Table.SelectRows(Source, each ([Status] = "Active"))
topics.output: Excel recalculates or cleans data instantly.

topics.title: 11. Keyboard Shortcuts & Best Practices
topics.content:
During a live interview, relying entirely on the mouse looks unprofessional. Memorize these to prove you are an advanced user.

  • Navigation: Ctrl + Arrow Keys jumps to the edge of data. Ctrl + Shift + Arrow highlights data instantly.
  • Formatting: Ctrl + 1 opens the Format Cells dialog. Ctrl + Shift + $ applies currency format. Ctrl + Shift + % applies percentage.
  • Actions: Alt + = instantly AutoSums a column. Ctrl + T converts data to a Table. F4 repeats your last action OR locks cell references in formulas.
topics.code:
# Essential Analyst Shortcuts
Ctrl + Arrow   = Jump to bottom of dataset
Alt + =        = AutoSum
Ctrl + PageUp  = Switch worksheet tabs
Ctrl + ;       = Insert current date hardcode
F2             = Enter cell edit mode
Ctrl + Shift + L = Toggle Filters
